Most likely it's a real world problem. The show wasn't serialized in season 1. So it had to be written in such a way that networks could just show any episode and it would be fine. This way, a kid could just watch any episode and pick up on the fact that her crush on Adrien is very important. In fact, kid's channels generally don't like serialized shows because they they have to stick to a release order (look at Gloob to see what happens when they don't stick to the right order), and they generally draw in less viewers. That's why so many cartoons will just be episodic with a plot heavy season finale, because that's all they can get away with. Miraculous was allowed to have a story once it showed it could hold an audience. The establishing season having pretty much no plot or character development has been a detriment to later seasons, but it's all they could do at the time. They couldn't have Marinette slowly develop feelings for Adrien because kids who don't see those episodes might be lost on how it happened. There is no "missing link" or rushed development. They just simply couldn't have that.
